Title: Start here
Paragraphs: 1 · Capture a chart and a blank white field with the same camera, exposure, lighting, focus, and image dimensions as your samples. Avoid clipped patches, glare, deep shadows, and automatic camera adjustments.

2 · Add your images to the session. Select the chart image and press Detect. Verify its detected type and patch overlay; if several faces are found, choose the intended Chart face. A wrong chart, orientation, or patch order invalidates calibration.

3 · Add the blank white image in the FFC area, not as a color chart. Enable the stages you need, then Fit + apply. Inspect stage previews, patch errors, and held-out validation before applying the model.

4 · Expand Model and choose Use loaded, then select a sample and run Apply model. A successful fit makes the model available but does not switch this mode automatically. Use matching capture conditions; save model JSON, reports, and corrected images.

Title: FFC · illumination
Paragraphs: Flat-field correction compensates for spatial brightness variation. Use a clean, matte blank white field captured in the same setup. For the sample photographs, use Blank.JPG as the FFC reference.

Inspect the chosen white-field region: it should exclude objects, edges, dirt, glare, and saturated areas. Surface degree and smoothing describe the illumination field; increasing complexity is not automatically more accurate.
FFC is spatial and cannot be represented by a 3D cube LUT. Reuse it only when camera geometry, framing, lighting, and image dimensions match.

FFC, GC, and WB currently require encoded sRGB input with D65 white. For other input RGB spaces, convert the image first or use CC alone; unsupported combinations are rejected rather than interpreted silently.

Title: GC & white balance
Paragraphs: Yes, GC uses the detected chart: it compares measured lightness from named neutral patches (after FFC when enabled) with the matching reference lightness. At least two usable named neutrals are required. It fits a monotonic curve anchored at black and white, not a fixed gamma exponent. There is no GC degree setting.

Apply model reuses the saved GC curve on every pixel; new sample images need no chart. A new fit, however, needs a detected chart with usable neutral patches. The stage order remains FFC → GC → WB → CC.

White balance adjusts the channel gains using neutral reference patches. Check that those patches are not clipped, occluded, or reflecting glare. A color-mapping model cannot recover information that the camera did not record.

Turn off stages you do not need, but evaluate the complete pipeline you intend to apply. Changing capture conditions requires recalibration; a low fitting error is not evidence that a model transfers to another setup.

Title: CC & neural networks
Paragraphs: Start with a simple fit and compare held-out error before increasing polynomial degree or model complexity. Linear and PLS fits provide useful baselines; NN is flexible but can overfit a small chart.

NN hidden layers accept a single width or one to four widths. Examples: ‘100’ or ‘100, 30’ or ‘[64, 32]’ or ‘[128, 64, 32]’. A comma-separated sequence specifies successive layers, not candidate models.

Choose Adam, SGD with momentum, or RMSProp. Batch normalization is optional and uses full-chart statistics for small datasets. Dropout ranges from 0 to 0.8; zero disables it. Keep a record of the optimizer, architecture, normalization, dropout, and training settings when comparing fits.

New NN models learn an identity-safe residual and keep their best non-regressing training checkpoint. That safeguards training, but does not guarantee low error on unseen images. Compare held-out results and inspect saturated colors, neutrals, shadows, and highlights.

Title: Color spaces & ΔE
Paragraphs: Input RGB space and white must describe the numeric pixels being supplied. Output RGB space describes the corrected pixel encoding. These are not cosmetic labels. Standard sRGB uses D65; selecting another white with the same primaries describes a custom variant.

With sRGB/D65 input, embedded ICC profiles are converted to working sRGB before correction. EXIF rotation is applied consistently to detection, sampling, thumbnails and exports. Explicit non-sRGB or custom-white input selections bypass ICC conversion and use the declared pixel encoding. Original previews honor ICC profiles for display. Corrected and stage previews are converted to display sRGB independently of exported bytes. Non-sRGB exports still need a downstream workflow that interprets their declared encoding correctly.

CIEDE2000 (ΔE00) measures perceptual distance in CIELAB with a common reference white. Lower is better, but a single mean hides outliers. Inspect the per-patch values, worst patches, and held-out validation as well as the mean.

A fitting score measures the calibration chart. Held-out error tests the CC mapping after GC/WB have been fitted; it is not validation of the whole pipeline on independent photographs. Low training error with high held-out error signals overfitting or an unsuitable chart reference. Apply-only images have no measured chart error. The app must not fabricate ΔE for them.

Reference values depend on chart type, patch order, illuminant, observer, and the physical chart. Published nominal values cannot certify your individual chart: aging, dirt, printing variation, glare, and illumination spectra remain sources of uncertainty. See the bundled color-science validation document for independent numerical fixtures and the exact tested scope.

Title: Session & catalog
Paragraphs: The catalog organizes available files; the session is your current working set. Select a session tile to make it active. The left and right preview arrows, or Alt+Left / Alt+Right, browse different session images—not the correction-stage previews.

Scroll the session and catalog areas to reach longer collections. Inspect the active filename before running, saving, or removing an item. Delete removes the selected item from the working session; it is not a command to erase your original image file.
Ctrl+O adds files; Ctrl+Shift+O adds a folder. Ctrl+Shift+S saves the session, and Ctrl+Alt+O loads it. Session persistence is separate from exporting corrected image files or reusable model JSON.

Title: Apply & save
Paragraphs: To apply an existing fit, expand Model and select Use loaded; load model JSON first if needed. Select the sample image and run Apply model. Fit from image is a different mode. No chart is needed on an apply-only image, but capture conditions must match. In Batch, choose Apply current model to reuse the model; Fit from chart calibrates each chart image separately.

Batch shows the active filename and its applicable FFC, GC, WB, CC and Save result indicators. Turn Preview results off to avoid generating previews for the batch; full-resolution output is still written. Existing completed results keep their captured model and settings when you change controls for the next operation. Drag the divider above the analysis section upward to enlarge the figures before inspecting or capturing them.

A completed GUI preview does not mean full-resolution files have been exported. Press Ctrl+S and choose Corrected (full size) for a full-resolution corrected image. FFC, GC, WB, and CC stage exports are preview-resolution images for inspection. Reports contain the chart measurements. Choose an output folder and Save selected; existing files require replacement confirmation. Model JSON preserves the reusable correction; a cube LUT contains only the non-spatial color mapping and excludes FFC.
Keep the source files unchanged and store outputs separately. Compare corrected results in a color-managed viewer before downstream measurement or publication.

Title: API & notebooks
Paragraphs: The same Rust worker used by the GUI accepts sequential newline-delimited JSON commands without opening a window. The bundled Python SDK and command-line interface provide a friendlier route for scripts, automation, and Jupyter notebooks; Python is optional for the desktop app.

Install the bundled wheel from python/ into your Python environment. Read api/README.md or docs/api/README.md beside the application. Pass root=the installed application folder to ColorCorrection or Client. Run the notebooks from https://github.com/collinswakholi/ColorCorrectionPackage_UI/tree/main/notebooks; the notebook files and photograph fixtures are supplied with the source, not the installer.

Start with ColorCorrection(Config(save_path="results"), root=app_folder), then run(Image="chart.jpg", White_Image="Blank.JPG") and predict_images(images=["sample.jpg"]). Config controls do_ffc, do_gc, do_wb and do_cc; options=CalibrationOptions(ffc=FFCOptions(...)) configures fitting. Config stage switches override the matching nested switches. GC and WB are fitted automatically; their public controls enable or disable those stages. The API guide shows editable FFC, CC and application options, typed results and model reload.

Use a separate worker per independent session and send one request at a time. Treat model state as belonging to that worker. A timeout must terminate the worker before another request, so a late reply cannot be mistaken for the next operation.

The API is a local process interface, not an internet server. The app does not open a network listener by default. Use explicit output directories and retain your model, configuration, chart reference, and reports for reproducibility.

Title: Troubleshooting
Paragraphs: No chart found: check focus, exposure, framing, and patch visibility, then press Detect again. Verify the detected chart type and overlay. Do not use Blank.JPG as the chart. Try a clear chart-bearing image from the same setup.

Poor correction despite a good mean ΔE: inspect individual patches and held-out errors; reduce fit complexity, check reference selection, and look for clipping, glare, mismatched color spaces, or changed lighting.
FFC artifacts: check the white-field region and dimensions, exclude edges or objects, and verify exposure consistency. Compare with FFC disabled to isolate the cause.

Worker or native-library error: open Processing settings, inspect the error, and restart the worker. Auto chart and plane detection use a compatible GPU and recover to CPU when needed. Select CPU for detection without a GPU; a forced GPU engine reports an error if unavailable. Use Check setup under Device details to inspect prerequisites and repair optional support. LUT processing uses wgpu with CPU recovery, while NN fitting remains on CPU. Inspect actual backend fields in API replies. Keep the executable, ONNX models, references, and GPU runtime libraries together.

Title: Research & citation
Paragraphs: This application builds on the stepwise workflow presented by Wakholi and colleagues: A systematic color correction pipeline for controlled-environment imaging. The Plant Phenome Journal 9, e70067 (2026). DOI: 10.1002/ppj2.70067. Published 11 March 2026.

The original ColorCorrectionPipeline Python package is available at https://pypi.org/project/ColorCorrectionPipeline/ with source at https://github.com/collinswakholi/ColorCorrectionPackage. Studio retains a familiar stepwise workflow and run/predict naming; its native implementation and typed results are not a drop-in replacement for the original package.

The research motivates evaluating the imaging setup together with correction, rather than treating a regression model as a substitute for controlled capture. The current application is an evolving implementation; its automatic GC and NN safeguards should not be assumed to reproduce every historical experimental setting.

Original research opens the publisher article. Study PDF opens your copy at docs/research/ppj2.70067.pdf; download the paper separately. The illustrated guide is available offline. Reference sources and interpretation limits are described in docs/color-science-validation.md.
